text.p: Healthsouth Corp. said Monday its profits rose more than tenfold in the fourth quarter and more than doubled in all of 1996, boosted by acquisitions and the strong growth of its existing businesses.

Healthsouth, the nation's largest provider of outpatient surgery and rehabilitative healthcare services, said profits rose to $62.4 million, or 37 cents a share, in the quarter ended Dec. 31 from $6 million, or 4 cents a share, in the year-ago period.
Revenues soared 21 percent to $642.8 million from $533.1 million.
Last year, Birmingham, Ala.-based Healthsouth bought Surgical Care Affiliates, Advantage Health Corp., Professional Sports Care Management and ReadiCare, Inc.

"In 1996, Healthsouth continued to focus on growing its national network of high-quality, cost-effective healthcare services to best serve managed care providers, self-insured employers and other payers," said Richard Scrushy, chairman.
"At the same time, through internal development, we opened or acquired 160 new facilities, which positioned Healthsouth to be the only healthcare provider in all 50 states."
In 1996, Healthsouth signed more than 1,100 new contracts with managed care companies and self-insured employers, bringing its total to over 2,300 contracts.
For full-year 1996, Healthsouth earned $220.8 million, or $1.35 a share, up from $92.5 million, or 62 cents a share, in 1995. Revenues grew to $2.4 billion from $2.0 billion.
Healthsouth's stock rose 50 cents to $42.50 on the New York Stock Exchange in late morning trading.
